newsitem.title: UK: Med gasoline and gas oil helped by futures strength.
newsitem.headline: Med gasoline and gas oil helped by futures strength.

text.p: Mediterranean gasoline and gas oil were helped on Tuesday by firmer futures but fuel oil slipped as demand was perceived to have fallen, traders said.
Gasoline held steady after a sharp rise in NYMEX unleaded futures and lingering demand from North America, north Africa and the eastern Med, primarily Turkey, traders said.
"There is a little demand popping up," said one trader at a major. "There is some demand from the U.S. for low octane and that could help strengthen the Med."
The arb from the Med to the States appeared nearly open.
Naphtha also was unchanged with little demand from NWE.

Gas oil was bolstered by futures that gained up to $3 a tonne, but there was signs of developing length. Traders said 0.2 pct Italian was starting to get well offered with quotes easing a touch to fob high +3-3.50.

There was more interest for 0.5 and 1.0 pct for the Canary Islands and IOC, and only one supplier. Traders said an offer was heard at fob high quotes +$3.50 for 1.0 pct with buying down at high fob quotes +$2-2.50.
Dealers said 0.05 pct was seeing 2-3 cargoes 10-20 dates availe ex-Italy and a 15-20 Skikda cargo available at numbers of around fob high EN590 quotes +$3.
There was active talk of low sulphur fuel cargoes moving to Italy but only one deal was actually believed done.
Demand for high sulphur bunker spec fuel appeared to wane and prices slipped accordingly to around $84/$85 cif.
Material was being offered at high cif +$2-$3 but deals were more likely to be done at mean cif to high cif flat.
"Its not as healthy in the Med for high sulphur as some people would have you believe," one trader said, pointing to cargoes being priced into Spain and Portugal.
